subject: Onboarding: model window & usage buckets (Finlytics)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Barnes <rachel@finlytics.com>, eng@finlytics.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Onboarding: model window & usage buckets (Finlytics)

Hi Rachel / Finlytics team,

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. As promised, I’m sending our initial recommendations for model candidates and the contextual / token buckets we think make sense for your use cases. This is intended to be a pragmatic shortlist to unblock the implementation sprint; we’ll iterate after the first week of traffic.

Top-line decisions we need from you this week:
- Confirm average prompt+response size target per product flow (we used current estimates in the attached spreadsheet).
- Confirm whether you need 32k-window context for the audit-history use case, or if a rolling 8k window with prefix caching suffices.

What I attached: model-shortlist-v1.csv (candidates with cost/latency tradeoffs), token-traffic-estimates.xlsx (per-flow monthly/day/peak buckets), onboard-MAP-draft.pdf (mutual action plan with milestones).

Shortlist rationale (quick):
1) Llama-2-70B (quantized int8) — best balance for long-context flows (up to 32k) when we enable KV prefix caching; higher infra cost but minimizes hallucination on long audit trails.
2) Mistral-22B (4-bit) — good latency/cost for shorter Q&A flows and API-heavy endpoints (~2k context).
3) OPT-13B hybrid-quant — lowest-cost candidate for high-throughput non-critical summarization where you can accept slightly higher variance in outputs.

Assumptions in the token workbook: 18k MAU, 45k daily active momentary users, average of 3 requests/user/day, avg prompt 650 tokens, avg response 420 tokens. Peak concurrency estimate: 120 concurrent RPS for the highest volume flow. Monthly baseline tokens: ~2.6B.

Next steps: Ben + Grace will propose instance sizing and a first-week canary config once Rachel confirms the context-window choice. If you want, we can reserve a small dedicated pool for the first month to stabilize latency.

Thanks — feel free to reply inline.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: model window & usage buckets (Finlytics)

Thanks Marissa — quick notes from infra/serving perspective: 

- For the 32k window option we recommend a split approach: route audit-history requests to Llama-2-70B (KV-cache enabled, dedicated pool) and route short chat/Q&A to Mistral-22B in a shared pool. That avoids over-provisioning 70B for all flows.
- If Finlytics wants to avoid a dedicated pool initially, we can run Llama-2-70B on burst-capacity dedicated nodes with auto-fallback to Mistral for non-critical queries. Latency will vary ~20–60ms depending on batch sizing.
- Sizing note: with your peak concurrency (~120 RPS) and the token counts Marissa listed, expect sustained GPU usage of roughly 4x A100-equivalents for the 70B path in worst-case; Mistral throughput needs ~1.5x. I put these as rough vCPU/GPU bands in the attached workbook.

I’ll draft a recommended canary config (instances, batch windows, cache TTLs) and share by EOD.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com

Adding a couple of prompts/quality notes:

- For audit-history extraction we recommend adding a deterministic post-processing step (rule-based sanity checks) rather than relying solely on model temperature. That keeps false-positive rates low without forcing the 70B for everything.
- If Finlytics expects many long-context retrievals, prioritize prefix/KV caching for common user histories — that reduces token re-encoding by ~30–40% in our experiments.
- Suggested quant profile: 70B → int8 (runtime with per-layer FP fallback) for correctness; Mistral → q4_0 for best throughput. I put an alternative q3 profile in the CSV too if you need lower cost.

I also added three test prompts (sheet tab: 'QA-cases') we’d like you to run in the first canary week to catch regression vs. your ground truth.

—Grace

Thanks Marissa + team — good alignment. A few clarifications from our side after checking with product/infra: 

- Audit-history: we do need effectively 30k–32k tokens for the full user timeline when the compliance view is generated (monthly scheduled exports + on-demand audit). For interactive view (UI) the 8k rolling window is fine. So the split routing Ben suggested sounds right.
- Token volumes: product team updated our numbers — MAU will likely be 26k not 18k for the second quarter post-launch; that increases the monthly baseline to ~3.8B tokens under current averages. We will try to optimize prompt templates before canary but assume the larger bucket for sizing.
- Procurement: we’re OK with a short-term dedicated pool for the 70B audit path for the canary month. Procurement asked for a one-page service commitment to attach to the PO — can you circulate a brief note with expected SLOs (p50/p95 latency targets) and fallback behavior?

I attached an internal note (not in this thread) with the updated MAU figures; I’ll share the concrete numbers in the workbook by EOD.

—Rachel
Rachel Barnes
Head of Product, Finlytics
rachel@finlytics.com

Subject: Re: Onboarding: model window & usage buckets (Finlytics)

Appreciate the update, Rachel — I’ve updated the token workbook with your 26k MAU projection and pushed a couple of conservative canary configs into the MAP:

- Canary plan (week 0–1):
  * Dedicated pool: 2x70B nodes (burst-capacity) for audit-history routes with prefix cache TTL = 6h
  * Shared pool: Mistral-22B (autoscale min 2 / max 8 nodes) for UI and Q&A flows
  * Fallback policy: if 70B queue > 30s average wait, route short summaries to Mistral at lower fidelity; flag in logs for post-hoc review.
- Latency targets to include in the one-page note: p50 < 350ms (70B, cached), p95 < 1.2s (70B non-cached), p50 < 220ms (Mistral). These are achievable with the config above; I’ll run a quick load sim and publish measured numbers tomorrow.

I attached a short SLO stub to the MAP and added the updated token numbers. Procurement — is that sufficient for the PO attachment? If not, let me know the exact fields you need.

Once procurement signs off, Ben can provision the canary nodes and Grace will schedule the QA prompt runs.

—Marissa
